html:
SMTO-ART-0013 — This Gateway can't send saved files to SMTO

GUID: 2ff732c1-3295-40ef-aa68-df1dfd5b6ecc
Slug: artifact-gateway-unsupported
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) is a version that can't share files with SMTO. Files from this step weren't added to the Task.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates below the Gateway list. Then find the Gateway this Task used in the list. Older Gateways lack the file-sharing feature SMTO needs here, and the check shows whether a newer version is ready.
  2. If that Gateway shows an Update to button, select it. Confirm with Update and restart only when no important work is running on that Gateway. The update stops that Gateway's running work, and unsaved work may be lost, before it installs the new version.
  3. If no update is offered or it says Manual update required, ask the person who manages that computer to reinstall the Gateway from the same release as the server. Some Gateways can only be updated on the computer itself.
  4. After updating, send the request again in a new message. SMTO checks a Gateway's features when a Task starts, so a new Task can use file sharing.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's details show Same release as server, and files from the new Task appear in Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't copy files from a different Gateway version over the installed one by hand; use the update buttons or the installer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected execution target cannot publish artifacts: its client has no artifact_operation, the Gateway answered 404 for /artifact/operation, an artifact-workspace path needs a workspace the target cannot provide, or task-temp publication is unsupported.

What this means

  • The selected client lacks artifact_operation, required workspace environment is absent, or the Gateway endpoint reports unsupported artifact publication. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • The selected client lacks artifact_operation, required workspace environment is absent, or the Gateway endpoint reports unsupported artifact publication.

How to diagnose it

  • Check advertised capability, matching Gateway version and workspace preparation separately from file existence.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's capability tags (artifact_workspace, artifact_discovery, artifact_temp_publication) under Settings › Setup › Gateways or in the run's gateway_capability_snapshot, and update the Gateway to the server's release through the supported update path. Start a new run afterwards so the capability snapshot is negotiated again.
  • Use a Gateway with the advertised artifact capability or update to a matching supported Gateway build.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported selected Gateway and workspace provide the intended publication operation.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
